steps.line: My dog Biscuit slipped his lead! He's scruffy and brown with one floppy ear. Someone saw him heading for {next}.
Three dogs begged for crusts here this morning. Which one's yours?
options: A sleek grey one with pointy ears
A scruffy brown one with one floppy ear
A fluffy white one in a tiny jumper
steps.wrong: That one went home with its owner. Yours sounded scruffier.
steps.right: That's him! He took a crust and ran off towards {next}.

steps.line: A chewed glove in a dug-up flower bed, with Biscuit-sized tooth marks. Muddy paw prints lead to {next}.
Got all his things? Good, he wouldn't budge without them. Last I saw he was trotting off to {next}.
There he is, tail going like mad. Mrs. Okafor says he picked you, so he's yours now.

hunt.line: Wet paws, muddy nose, happy as anything. Biscuit won't go home without his things: {items}. Split up, then meet me back here!

steps.line: This old map fell out of a 1985 yearbook, signed by a class called the Comets. The first mark is at {next}.
My Comets buried a capsule! After, they argued for an hour somewhere that smelled of fresh bread. Start there.

steps.hint: Where the Comets argued over bread
steps.line: The owner laughs: those kids argued here about where to bury it, then marched off to {next}.
There are three old marker posts along here. Which one does your map mean?
options: The one with a star painted on
The one with a comet scratched on
The one with a fish carved in
steps.wrong: Hmm. What did that class call themselves again?
steps.right: The comet post! Its little arrow points straight at {next}.

steps.line: Key, photo and the combination, all here. I put the tin back at {next} where it was buried, go open it!
A rusty tin full of letters from 1985. Everyone takes one to read.

hunt.line: I dug the capsule up, but it's locked, and the class hid what opens it: {items}. Split up and meet me back here.

steps.line: It's Grandpa Lou's 90th and nothing's ready! He loves lemon and can't stand chocolate. Can you get the cake from {next}?
I baked three party cakes today and lost all the labels. Which one is Lou's?
steps.wrong: Hmm, didn't Priya say what Lou likes?
steps.right: Lemon drizzle, done. Priya also wanted music, try the busker at {next}.

steps.line: A party? I'm in. My cousin Dee has fireworks, find her at the spot every postcard of this town shows.
Cousin Dee waves a box of fireworks. Lou's friend Mabel is doing decorations at {next}, she sounds stressed.
Bunting, candles, guest book, perfect. Lou loves the view, so the party is at {next}.
SURPRISE! Lou nearly drops his hat. The whole street came to watch the fireworks.

hunt.line: Lou's party still needs {items}. Split up, grab them, and meet me back here!

steps.line: The Night Owls haven't played in 30 years. Our drummer Dot works at {next}, she drums on everything in reach.
Dot? Three of us are on shift. Which one do you mean?
options: The one drumming on the ticket machine
steps.wrong: Nope. Didn't Ray say something about her hands?
steps.right: Dot spins a pen like a drumstick: a reunion? About time. Lenny busks wherever people wait for trains.

steps.hint: Where Lenny busks for waiting folk
steps.line: Lenny plays a riff without looking up. Still got it. Our singer Marisol runs a little place at {next}.
Sticks, strings and my lyrics, we're a band again. Fine, one show! Tell everyone to meet at {next}.
Count it in! The Night Owls play their comeback show, and the crowd sings along.

hunt.line: We can't play without our gear: {items}. Split up and meet me back here.

steps.line: "Where old things sleep and new eyes wake, you found me. Now seek the place of bells and quiet stones."
A chalk mark on the step: "Green and wide where children play, a clue lies hid at {next}, go that way."
Under a bench, a folded note: "The river knows where treasure goes. Ask at {next}."
"Three torn pieces, one whole map. The X sits under {next}, so off you tap."
Tucked under the span, an old chest full of gold and diamonds. Not bad.

hunt.line: "Three torn pieces, scattered wide: {items}. Bring them here and set them side by side."

steps.line: Psst. I'm Edith, the ghost in the lavender coat, don't scream. I never sent my letters. The first goes where every letter in town is sorted.
The postmaster reads the envelope: Edith! She was my grandmother's friend. Her sister's family lives near {next}.
A letter from Aunt Edith's ghost? Prove it. What colour did she always wear?
steps.wrong: Not her. Edith told you herself, remember?
steps.right: Lavender, always. Thank you. She had tea every Sunday at {next}, they'll remember her.

steps.line: Her rose, her watch, her teacup. Edith had tea here every Sunday, and she said she'd rest at {next}.
All my letters delivered. Thank you, friends. Edith smiles and fades into the light.

hunt.line: Edith left three keepsakes for her goodbye: {items}. Split up, fetch them, and meet back here.

steps.line: A meteor shower tonight, but the town's too bright to see it. Light my first beacon at the highest spot you can get to.
Beacon one, lit! A night owl up here says Dr. Lin wants the next one at {next}.
The beacon's crystal lens, dropped in the grass. Beacon two glows. The last one's at {next}.
All lit, and the kit's here! Dr. Lin is setting up at {next}. Hurry, it's starting.
Look up! The sky fills with falling stars. Make a wish.

hunt.line: Dr. Lin forgot half her kit: {items}. Split up and meet back here before the sky starts!

steps.line: Mayor Whiskers is missing before the ceremony! She's ginger with a white tip on her tail. She was last seen near {next}.
Her Honour took a sardine and strolled off to nap somewhere green, with flowers to roll in.

steps.hint: Green, with flowers to roll in
steps.line: Squashed tulips and ginger fur. A gardener points: the mayor wandered off to {next}.
Three cats napped on my steps today. Which was the mayor?
options: The black cat with a bell
The grey cat with a bow
The ginger cat with a white-tipped tail
steps.wrong: That one's just a regular cat. What did the clerk say she looks like?
steps.right: That's Her Honour. She's off to the ceremony, but the usher at {next} says her regalia's gone.

steps.line: Crown, sash and golden sardine, all present. The mayor's waiting at {next}, go crown her!
Found her! Mayor Whiskers is crowned for another term, purring the whole time.

hunt.line: The ceremony needs the mayor's regalia: {items}. Split up and meet me back here.

steps.line: This bottle washed up: "To Arthur, from Rose, 1962." Whoever keeps the town's old records might know them.

steps.hint: Where the old records are kept
steps.line: An archivist blows dust off a file: Rose Bell! Arthur still lives near {next}. He never goes out without his flat cap.
Arthur? Three old gents come here every day. Which one do you want?
options: The one in the flat cap
steps.wrong: That's Harold. The archivist said something about a hat, didn't she?
steps.right: Arthur reads the letter twice. Rose? She always loved {next}. Could you find her?

steps.line: Our letter, our photo, the shell from our first day out. Tell Arthur to meet me at {next}.
Two old friends meet again on the bridge, laughing like it was 1962.

hunt.line: Arthur kept my letter? Before I see him I want to bring {items}. Split up, and meet me back here?

steps.line: La-la! I dropped my shiny things all over town. The first is at {next}!
A little blue thing took a cookie and left a bell. It flew off to where the trains come and go.

steps.hint: Where the trains come and go
steps.line: A conductor holds up a ribbon from platform two. The allay went humming towards {next}.
A music disc, still warm from the allay's pocket, if allays have pockets. Singing drifts over from {next}.
It sang in our class all morning! Now everything's back, and it's waiting for you at {next}.
All its shiny things back! The allay twirls around you and decides to stay.

hunt.line: The allay's last shiny things are scattered: {items}. Split up and meet me back here!

steps.line: The Founders' Festival is tonight and the banners aren't up! The founders' colours are green and gold. Start at {next}.
Three boxes of banners got delivered. Which ones are ours?
steps.wrong: Those are for the football club. The planner told you the colours.
steps.right: Green and gold, up they go. The art club kids at {next} have the lanterns.

steps.line: We painted lanterns! Hang them where everyone passes on the way in by train.
A busy conductor helps hang the lanterns, beaming. The planner's waiting at {next}, she sounds worried.
Lanterns, flag, drum, we're ready. Everyone's gathering at {next}!
Lanterns glow, music plays and the Founders' Festival begins. You made it happen.

hunt.line: We're short on festival things: {items}. Split up and meet me back here!

steps.line: My secret garden needs sunflower, poppy and cornflower seeds, one from every park. Start at {next}.
A packet of sunflower seeds, with a ranger's note: poppies grow best at {next}.
Poppy seeds, here, the sparrows can spare them. For the last kind ask the florist at {next}.
Mrs. Greene sent you? Then you know which seeds she's still missing.
steps.wrong: You've got those already, check your pockets.
steps.right: Cornflowers, and a little extra. Her old tools are with her neighbour at {next}.

steps.line: Shears, trowel and the magic stuff. Her garden's hidden at {next}, don't tell a soul.
You plant the seeds and the whole garden bursts into bloom.

hunt.line: Mrs. Greene needs her old tools too: {items}. Split up and meet me back here.

steps.line: This town once had an iron guardian, and its parts got scattered. One ended up in the lost and found where trains stop.

steps.hint: A lost and found where trains stop
steps.line: A rail worker drags out a huge iron arm. Funny, the other arm turned up near {next}.
There it is, the second iron arm, heavy as a piano. The heart was kept safe at {next}.
The golem's heart, still warm, and now all its parts. Rebuild it at {next}.
Clank by clank, the guardian stands again and gives you a poppy.

hunt.line: The golem needs three more things to wake: {items}. Split up and meet me back here.

steps.line: The great picnic bake-off is today and I'm out of everything, even my recipe card! Wheat first, from {next}.
Wheat, freshly cut. Amara dropped a card on her way past {next}, have a look around there.
The recipe card: honey and cinnamon sponge, underlined twice. The cafe at {next} has spices.
I've got three jars open. Which spice does Amara's recipe want?
steps.wrong: Close, but check that recipe card again.
steps.right: Cinnamon, a whole jar. Eggs next, the grocer at {next} keeps the best.

steps.line: Blanket, honey, berries, and a dozen eggs from me. Careful now. The picnic is at {next}!
Everyone shares cake on the grass. Amara declares it a tie, so everyone wins.

hunt.line: Amara phoned, the picnic needs {items}. Split up and meet me back here!

steps.line: I dropped all my postcards around town! The first one shows {next}.
A postcard with a footprint on it. The picture on the front is {next}.
Found another one in my bin. It shows the spot where you'd stand for the best photo in town.

steps.hint: The best photo spot in town
steps.line: A cyclist hands you a postcard of this very view. The last one shows {next}, not far.
Last postcard, and the suitcase stuff too. The tourist is waiting at {next}.
All my postcards! Here, take this painting of the town. Sign it, it's yours.

hunt.line: Wait, the tourist's suitcase burst open too! Help find {items}. Split up and meet me back here.

steps.line: Biscuit! Remember me? He's yours now, but he still drags everyone to his old haunts. He's sniffing towards {next}.
Same as last time, a crust for the good boy. He buried his tennis ball near {next} once, he's off to check.
His old tennis ball, chewed and proud. Now he's tugging towards where that fisher let him get his paws wet.

steps.hint: Where Biscuit got his paws wet
steps.line: The fisher from last time waves: you muddy legend. She reckons he'll want a nap at {next}.
Biscuit flops in the shade with his ball between his paws and snores. Best walk ever, apparently.
Is that Biscuit? He dug up my flower bed, remember! Kidding, all forgiven. He's in the pet show, sign him in at {next}.
Biscuit's in! He needs a trick. Sam says he learned one for crusts, ask at the place Biscuit begged for crusts.
Sam laughs: his trick? He sits, spins twice, then sneezes. Every time. The show's judge is at {next}.
Final round! What's Biscuit's trick, then?
options: He sits, spins twice, then sneezes
He balances a biscuit on his nose
steps.wrong: Biscuit looks at you, puzzled. That's not his trick, ask yourself what Sam said.
steps.right: Spin, spin, achoo! The crowd loses it. Prizes are handed out at {next}.

steps.line: Biscuit wins Best Sneeze, a prize we made up on the spot. He wears the rosette all day and won't let anyone touch it.
It's Biscuit's birthday! Same day I found him as a pup. Everyone from his adventures is coming. Sam's baking at {next}.
One dog cake, carrot, no chocolate, dogs can't have chocolate. The fisher has his present, she's at {next}.
A brand new squeaky bone with a bow, hidden for Biscuit to sniff out. Ms. Patel has party hats at {next}.
Hats on! Quick, before the cake comes out: what must Biscuit never eat?
steps.wrong: That one's fine for him. Sam warned you about one thing.
steps.right: Right, no chocolate, and Sam's cake is safe. Bring the birthday boy to {next}!

steps.line: Everyone sings. Biscuit eats his cake in one bite, spins twice and sneezes, for old times' sake.
Remember our comeback show? Now we're doing a little tour! Every gig opens with Moonlight on the Ring Road. Dot has posters at {next}.
Posters, fresh off the printer, but I dropped the pins. Stick one up at {next}, everyone reads the board there.
The box of pins! Poster up, a bit wonky. Lenny's warming up at {next} for tonight.
I'm so nervous I forgot the set list. What do we open with?
steps.wrong: No, that's the encore. Ray told you, didn't he?
steps.right: That's the one! Gig one's at {next}, Marisol's waiting.

steps.line: Gig one of the tour, and a full crowd of twelve. Marisol calls them the best twelve people in the world.
Gig two is tonight and my voice is gone, listen, croak. Ray says his gran's cure fixes anything, he's at {next}.
Gran's cure: warm honey, a lemon and a woolly scarf. Never fails, she sang till 96. Honey's sold at {next}.
Last jar of honey, it's yours. No lemons, but Lenny bought one, he's busking near the trains again.
Lenny hands over a slightly squashed lemon. Dot's been knitting something at {next}.
One scarf, done. Before you go, do you have all of Gran's cure?
steps.wrong: Ha, that's my cure for Mondays. What did Ray say?
steps.right: All three, then. Marisol's warming up at {next}, go!

steps.line: Honey, lemon, scarf, and her voice comes back mid-song. Gig two's a hit, and Lenny's glad he didn't have to sing.
Last gig of the tour, and I've lost my lucky drumsticks again, the ones you found at the reunion. I had them at {next}.
The lucky drumsticks, right where she left them. Lenny's pacing at {next}.
Last gig, I'm a wreck. Ray wants to play where the whole town is in view, he's up there now.

steps.hint: Where the whole town is in view
steps.line: Ray admits it's far too windy up here for the amps. We'll play at {next} and come back up after for the view.
The last gig, and the whole town turns up. Ray says it's not goodbye, the Night Owls just need a nap.
Every year I count the town's pigeons and every year they refuse to sit still. Start at {next}, they love the crumbs.
Fourteen out back, and Duchess, the one with the white wing. She's the boss. She sits on the most famous spot in town.

steps.hint: The most famous spot in town
steps.line: There's Duchess, white wing and all, looking very important. Gerald dropped his tally sheet near {next}.
The tally sheet, all little ticks and one doodle of a pigeon in a hat. Bring it to Gerald at {next}.
Before I write it in the book: which bird runs the flock?
options: Steve, who only has one foot
steps.wrong: Steve wishes. Who did the shop owner say was the boss?
steps.right: Duchess, of course. Fifteen pigeons, a record year! Celebrate with me at {next}.

steps.line: Gerald reads out the final count to nobody but you, and the pigeons coo along. You're now honorary census takers.
I locked my best trick in a puzzle box and forgot the code, ta-da. I hid the first number with a friend at {next}.
He paid me in card tricks for years. The first number is 3. The second is hidden where people wait for trains.
Scratched under a bench: a tiny top hat and the number 7. The last number is with the kids at {next}.
Fennimore did a show here once and left a card. The number on the back is 1! His assistant Gwen has the box at {next}.
The box clicks politely. The three numbers, in order, please?
steps.wrong: The box makes a sad little buzz. Try them in the order you found them.
steps.right: Click! The box opens and Gwen gasps. Fennimore wants the big reveal at {next}.

steps.line: Out of the box flutters a paper dove, and that's the whole trick. Fennimore bows like it's the best night of his life.
Yusuf and I have played one chess game for 40 years, by note. My move: knight to F3. Take it to him at {next}.
Knight to F3? The cheek. My reply is tucked in a chess book, at the place in town that lends books for free.

steps.hint: Where books are lent for free
steps.line: Inside the chess book, a note: bishop takes knight. Bernard's granddaughter Ana is at {next}.
Grandpa will want to know what Yusuf played before he even says hello. What was it?
steps.wrong: Hmm, that's not what the note in the book said.
steps.right: Bishop takes his knight? Grandpa will groan for a week. He's waiting at {next}.

steps.line: Bernard groans, then laughs and calls Yusuf over. For the first time in 40 years they finish the game face to face. It's a draw.
The charity duck race starts soon and my box of rubber ducks fell off my bike! Number 42, the one with a crown, is the favourite. Start at {next}.
Rubber duck number 7, dusty but still smiling. A kid says more ducks bounced towards {next}.
Ducks rolled in here all morning. I kept three, which one's the race favourite?
options: The one in a sailor hat
The one with a little crown
steps.wrong: That one's cute, but Bea told you what the favourite wears.
steps.right: Number 42, the champion. Bea's helper at {next} is rounding up the rest.

steps.line: Every duck accounted for! Bea's starting the race at {next}, let's go.
The ducks bob off downstream and number 42 wins by a beak. The race raises enough for a new park bench.

hunt.line: Three ducks are still loose: {items}. Split up, grab them and meet me back here!
